Torah #248 is a single-paragraph aphorism with a purely causal/consequential structure. The Rebbe states one thing: stories of tzaddikim (סִפּוּרִים מִצַּדִּיקִים) are very great, because they awaken the heart with burning desire for God. The mechanism is the reshimu — the spiritual impression the tzaddik made through his service — which is reactivated when his stories are told and produces arousal toward God.

The test for a new package requires: '3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text that form an independent domain.' Torah #248 does not meet this bar:

1. There are zero occurrences of 'בְּחִינַת' in the source text.
2. There are zero 'נִקְרָא' usages establishing parallel-aspects identity.
3. The three nouns in the teaching — סִפּוּרִים מִצַּדִּיקִים, רְשִׁימוּ, and הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַלֵּב — are linked by 'כִּי' (because) and 'עַל יְדֵי' (through/by means of), which are eitza markers, not bechina markers.
4. The teaching is intentionally compact: it makes a single practical declaration without developing a thematic topology of parallel-aspects identities.

Conclusion: no bechina subgraph exists, no connected components can be found, no packages — existing or new — arise from Torah #248. The entire content is captured by the single eitza edge already in the dataset (edge 2282).
